summary: Luxembourg is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (ETIAS is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a €90 Schengen short-stay visa, applied for via Luxembourg's missions or the Schengen partners that represent it abroad.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Luxembourg?
faq.answer: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely. US, UK, Canadian, Japanese and around 60 other visa-exempt nationalities can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area (ETIAS is not yet in operation). Everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa before traveling.

faq.question: How much does a Luxembourg Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11, allowing up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries. Guichet.lu does not publish a fee for the national long-stay (Type D) visa; it says long-stay visas are issued only by Luxembourg or Belgian embassies.

faq.question: Where do I apply if Luxembourg has no embassy in my country?
faq.answer: Under the EU Visa Code, one Schengen state can represent another for visa applications where the other has no consulate.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Luxembourg?
faq.answer: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers across the Schengen Area is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once mandatory, the €20 online authorization will be required before boarding.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Luxembourg without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area. EU and EFTA citizens do not need a visa.
